cells.tense: The steady one is here where what is already yours comes forward, shaping it with both hands now.
cells.act: ask how it feels to them and stay with the answer
cells.ask: Ask someone how something felt for them, and keep your attention there while they tell it — no fixing, no taking it on.
cells.core:
Where something finished has to be held steady, you steady it with your hands rather than a speech — shaped, kept, made to outlast the week it was made in. People can feel that you mean it. Building and tending are not two jobs in you, and the work comes out solid because of it.

What wakes alongside the work is how you meet whoever stands next to it. Someone near you will feel something this week — about what you are making, about what it costs, something of their own — and your instinct is to reach for a tool. Stay instead. Ask how it is for them, and keep your attention there while they tell it, without improving anything. Carrying attention is lighter than carrying weight and harder to fake. Noticing them and yourself at the same time is what keeps strong hands from going cold.
cells.sheetLine: You build the lasting thing and stay where it moves.

cells.tense: The steady hands are braced against a future that can't be written in, holding every beam before it bears load.
cells.act: weigh what it costs them against what it gives
cells.ask: When heat rises between you and someone, pause a beat — name what it cost that person, what it gave, then settle it fairly.
cells.core:
Where you build, you are already carrying the finished thing before it exists — every joint decided, every load imagined, every future held because someone has to hold it. The hands are still good. They are holding more than is here yet, and what they hold is starting to outweigh what is real.

Weigh it before you carry it. That is the oldest fair-minded move in your kit, and it is available. The next time heat rises between you and another person, pause a beat. Name what actually happened, then what it actually cost, then what it actually gave. This is the same judgment you run on materials, turned on a feeling. When the scale settles, the hands come back to the beam in front of them, and the building holds without force.
cells.sheetLine: You are carrying tomorrow's weight with today's hands.

cells.tense: The steady one waits at a door already closed, hands still on the last thing finished.
cells.act: release what is done and keep what is not
cells.ask: Something you finished is still being carried. Put it down tonight, and put it down again tomorrow.
cells.core:
Somewhere along the way, letting go stopped arriving by itself. What you completed, you finished; then instead of turning toward the next thing, you stayed at the door of the last one, hands still on it. The skill is there. It is waiting on a step that isn't coming.

Not every plank needs a second nail — that is what your hands already know and what they have stopped trusting. This week, take something done: a job, a repair, a favor, a stretch of time you gave someone. Mark it finished in whatever way is yours, and close it out. Something else is standing on the floor where the finished thing was, and it only shows up once the old one is actually put away. Nobody is asking you to drop the work. Only to take your hands off the rail.
cells.sheetLine: You are holding something that ended without you noticing.

cells.tense: The steady one is already shaping what gets made, and does not count the judgment as owned.
cells.ask: At the next choice that lands, give one plain reason for taking it that way before you move on.
cells.core:
You decide what to make and how to hold it, and it does not register as deciding. It registers as standing at the bench until the right way shows itself — solid, honest, and not something you claim. The work comes out yours. The judgment gets filed under the work.

No one taps you on the shoulder at the moment the call gets made; it is too quiet for that. So the live question is what you would build if the call counted as yours. Start with one sentence: when a choice lands this week, give one plain reason for the way you took it before moving on. Small and level. A thing made by someone who knows it is theirs gets a different kind of care, and there is more of that care in you than is being used.
cells.sheetLine: You decide, and the decision gets filed under the work.
